traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements in docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are implemented and verified:
- Rule Naming: 'prefer-supports-annotation' is the primary rule name, and 'prefer-implements-annotation' is a deprecated alias with meta.replacedBy pointing to the primary. This is wired in src/index.ts and validated by tests and documentation. - Optional Warning & Configurable Enforcement: The rule is not included in the recommended/strict presets, so it is effectively 'off' by default. Tests confirm it can be configured with severities 'off'/'warn'/'error' for both the primary rule and the alias, matching REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, and the story’s configuration examples. - Auto-fix Support & Single Story Conversion: Implementation only auto-fixes simple single-story @story + @req blocks (including single-story/multi-req) into a single @supports line. Tests explicitly cover these patterns and verify the produced output. - Multi-story Detection & Cannot-auto-fix Cases: The rule detects mixed @story/@req/@supports usage and multiple @story paths in the same comment, emits specific messageIds ('cannotAutoFix', 'multiStoryDetected'), and intentionally does not attempt auto-fix. This aligns with REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT and the story’s "Cannot auto-fix" examples. - Preserve Order / Format & Valid Output: Auto-fix uses indentation-aware replacement to preserve the surrounding JSDoc structure and tags, only rewriting the legacy annotation lines. It bails out on complex or ambiguous formats, ensuring that fixes are conservative and produce annotations that pass existing @supports validation rules. Tests and docs demonstrate correct placement (after description, before params) and confirm no malformed output. - Both Formats Valid & Backward Compatibility: With the rule disabled (default), behavior of @story/@req/@supports is governed solely by the existing validation rules. Even when enabled, comments that only use one style are ignored, so legacy annotations remain valid and not forcibly migrated. This satisfies REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION and the AC "Both Formats Valid". - Documentation: There is a dedicated rule doc (docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md) plus a section in user-docs/migration-guide.md explaining the migration rule, its auto-fix behavior, and how to opt in via configuration. These match the story’s examples and guidance.
Given the current code, tests, and documentation, the story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS is fully implemented. The unchecked checkbox for "Rule Naming" in the story file does not reflect the actual implementation state; the implementation and tests clearly satisfy that criterion.
